dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals convicted of sex offenses against minors who seek labor organization leadership or consulting roles.
dimensions.evidence: prohibits an individual convicted of a sex offense against a minor from serving in a leadership position for a labor organization

dimensions.assessment: Barring individuals from specific professional leadership and consulting roles for 13 years represents a major career impact for those affected.
dimensions.evidence: for 13 years after the conviction or imprisonment for the offense

dimensions.assessment: No federal spending, revenue, or economic effects are stated or implied in the source.
Amends a specific section of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959 to add a new category of disqualifying offenses.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act of 1959

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change with ongoing 13-year individual prohibitions taking effect nationally.
dimensions.evidence: shall take effect 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act

missing_information: Exact number of individuals currently holding or seeking these positions who have such convictions.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands existing federal prohibitions to bar individuals convicted of sex offenses against minors from holding union leadership or consulting positions for 13 years, affecting a specific criminal and professional demographic.
